messages:
ashley: Heads up — planning a rolling maintenance for prod GPU pools next Tuesday 02:00-06:00 UTC. Goal: apply kernel + firmware patch that reduces thermal spikes we saw last month. This will require cordon+drain of ~120 nodes across us-west1 and eu-central, staggered in 20-node cohorts.

mike: rough expected impact? will Dedicated customers be affected?

ashley: Dedicated pools have isolation but their workload may fall back to hosted in rare saturation cases. Expect transient latency + occasional 503s for short tails if backfill hits capacity limits. We'll keep >=20% spare capacity for 95th pct SLA.

raj: are we doing spot/ondemand churn for backfill? cost-wise we should prefer ondemand for the canaries.

ashley: yes — plan is ondemand for first two cohorts (canaries), then spot backfill for remaining to save cost. if queue depth rises >15s we'll pause and swap to ondemand.

infra-bot: Reminder: runbook link https://internal.redwood/ops/maintenance-runbooks#gpu-rolling. Auto-scaling policy must be set to manual-scale during each cohort drain.

ashley: scheduling notes: us-west1 cohorts start 02:00, eu-central cohorts start 05:00 UTC to avoid EU peak. apac excluded this window to avoid weekday morning impact there.

eva: can someone post the exact drain command and kube flags we should use? want to include in runbook so oncall can copy+pasta.

mike: use this: ```kubectl cordon NODE && kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --timeout=20m``` also run `rdw-node-health check $NODE` before uncordon.

oncall-jun: noted. i'll be primary for first two canaries and will monitor tokenized latency dashboards + prefix cache hit rates. set alerts: token_latency_p95 > 350ms for 5m and cache_hit_rate drop >10% -> page.

raj: small ask — can we pre-warm KV cache for the cohorts by replaying top-50 prefixes for model-serving? that avoids cold-start token costs. there is a script at /ops/scripts/hydrate_kv.sh but it needs service account perms.

ashley: good idea. raj — can you coordinate perms with security and put a short note in the runbook. we'll budget an extra ~3% runtime cost for prewarm traffic but should cut tail latency.

mike: ops nit: remember to toggle routing policy to prefer eu-variants during eu cohort to avoid cross-region egress spikes. update the routing-config and keep version pinned for 4 hours.

ashley: final checklist I'm putting in #incidents 24h before: cohorts list, oncall roster, rollback window (30m), canary metrics (p95 latency, error rate, cache hit), and cost burn estimate (~$2.2k). Any objections? :think: :clock1:

eva: no objections. I'll run a dry-run on staging tomorrow at same cadence.

raj: volunteering for post-mortem doc if anything regresses.

ashley: thanks — i'll send calendar invites + update the maintenance page. infra-bot, please post a reminder 12h before.

infra-bot: Scheduled reminder posted to #eng-infra at 12h and 1h before window.
